headline: Panthers' Cooper Black, all 6-9 of him, becomes NHL's tallest goalie
take:
Per ESPN, Florida's Cooper Black, who is 6-9, is now the NHL's tallest goalie. He is listed two inches taller than the previous holders of the mark: Ben Bishop, Ivan Fedotov, Mads Sogaard and Mikko Koskinen.

Our numbers don't have a goalie line on Black yet, so his height tells us nothing about how he performs. What we can say is where he'd be stepping into. FLA sits at 5-3-2 with 12 points through 10 games, and so far this season it controls 52.8% of expected goals, a measure of shot quality that credits the team for the chances it creates and allows. At five-on-five that share climbs to 55%. The weak spot is finishing: FLA has scored 2.1 fewer goals than its chances would predict, and its goaltending has saved 0.4 fewer goals than expected, so the results trail the play. A goalie who steadies that save number would help the record catch up to how the team is actually playing. For now, treat Black as a curiosity until he has a sample.
